title: Why do trends even exist?
hook: If everyone can see the news at once, why does price drift for weeks?
metaphor: Imagine buying every apple in the country. You cannot do it in one go. You buy a truckload a day for weeks, and the price creeps up the whole time.
body: Big funds move billions. There is never enough for sale at one price.
So they buy a slice at a time, quietly, for weeks or months.
That slow steady buying is what you see as a trend.
This is why a direction can last long after the news that started it.

live.template: Right now stocks are {spx_dir} over the last 3 months ({spx_3mo}%). That is one of these slow moves in progress.

caveat: Trends end without warning. A long move is not a promise the next day goes the same way.
